title: Memory Masterclass: Make Your AI Agents Remember What They Do! — Mark Bain, AIUS
talk_summary: The talk argues agent memory should be graph-structured and causal, then demos graph/vector memory tools: Cogni semantic graph, Neo4j MCP memory server, Zep temporal graph with domain schemas, and a graph chat arena. Practical mechanisms are recall-before/log-after memory, typed business-domain entities, temporal action history, and per-graph isolation; most claims are vendor demos without measured results.

takeaways.what_they_do: A Neo4j-backed MCP memory server plus a system prompt makes the agent recall related memories before each turn and create/update entities, observations, and relationships after the turn.
takeaways.evidence_quote: at each interaction, it tries to recall memories that are related to the user prompt. And then at the end of this interaction, it will create new entities

takeaways.what_they_do: They reject generic fact dumping and define business-domain entity types, fields, and rules, then filter retrieval by node type instead of relying on semantic similarity.
takeaways.evidence_quote: semantic similarity is not business relevance

takeaways.what_they_do: They propose episodic/temporal memory of shell commands and events across sessions/machines so an agent can see what happened historically.
takeaways.evidence_quote: episodic memory the sort of temporal memory of what was happening in this shell historically

takeaways.what_they_do: In Q&A they say physically separate graphs per user works well; Neo4j also supports role-based access controls.
takeaways.evidence_quote: if you isolate per graph per user or kind of keep it like very physically separate for us it works really works well

takeaways.what_they_do: They built a chat arena over one graph to switch between memory implementations and compare how graphs are created and retrieved.
takeaways.evidence_quote: It's just one Neo4j graph on the back end and all of these technologies that can be tested how the graphs are being created and retrieved.
